solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unprepared following fraud, go bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken apart, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone caught out after a swindle goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' is the anagram signal; the abbreviation for 'following' joins the pool rather than standing outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught off guard means taken by surprise, so not ready.

clue.text: It's only just succeeded in light show

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the two words that follow it

parts.note: fair hair or skin is light in colour
a fair is a show or exhibition, as in a trade fair
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A light show that went off well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S between FAIR and FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is used to insist something is reasonable and even-handed, simply just.

clue.text: Making a faux pas of working clothes

indicators.note: used as a verb: the outer word dresses, wraps round the inner one

parts.note: a going concern is one that works
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gaffe made about what to wear at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, meaning wraps round; 'working' as in a going concern.
explanation.definitionFit: To goof is to blunder, so goofing is committing a gaffe.

clue.text: Own flat, with no parking, bit reduced

indicators.note: the parking letter is taken away from the flat word

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the word for bit is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a mite is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: An owner-occupier's flat, without parking, shrinks a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops P from PAD to leave AD; 'reduced' cuts MITE to MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, as admit means.

clue.text: Built for rearing, striking earth mother

indicators.note: striking out a letter removes it from the reversed word
in a down clue rearing means rising up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: made means built
E is the electrician's abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Something constructed for raising young, hitting an earth-mother figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for rearing' turns MADE into EDAM; 'striking' removes E (earth). 'earth mother' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the female parent of an animal, especially a horse.

clue.text: Daring to pull out close to motorway

parts.note: to pluck is to pull out, as with feathers or a string

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bold manoeuvre pulling out near the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone plucky has courage and nerve.

clue.text: Establish clan having moved from south of France

parts.note: to prove is to establish as true

indicators.note: the letters of clan have been moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A clan relocates from the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having moved' rearranges CLAN to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Provence is a region of southern France; its adjective describes things native there.

clue.text: Scottish singer, being upset, had to give a hoot

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Lulu is the Glasgow-born pop singer of Shout fame
to have a meal is to eat, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A Scottish singer, upset, had to show she cared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns LULU over to ULUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail, as an owl's hoot or a mourner's cry.

clue.text: Characters in burka bullied here?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A city where a veiled woman was bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is Afghanistan's capital, where the burka is widely worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabul is the Afghan capital, a place where women in burkas are seen.

clue.text: Daughters smothered in lotion lying about pool

indicators.note: the daughter letter is covered over by the lotion word
about means turned round, so the lotion word reads backwards

parts.note: oil is a lotion for the skin
D is the abbreviation for daughter(s)

explanation.surface: Daughters slathered in sun cream lounging by the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying about' turns OIL into LIO; 'smothered in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Quiet child unable to finish extra-large humbug

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum

indicators.note: the child word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a boy is a child
jumbo means very large

explanation.surface: A silent child who cannot finish an enormous sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is also a British boiled sweet, which feeds the picture; here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug is nonsense or deceptive talk, which is what gibberish ritual talk amounts to.

clue.text: Help sheepdog exposed by position

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, the dog's name loses its covering

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of film and television
a stance is a position taken

explanation.surface: A sheepdog shows its worth by where it stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips L and E from LASSIE to leave ASSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is aid or support.

clue.text: Reindeer stunted if ground more impoverished

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
stunted means cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A reindeer whose growth fails on poor grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' takes the final R off REINDEER; 'ground' rearranges REINDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means poor, so the comparative means poorer.

clue.text: Rod driven round by boring porter?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
X is the multiplication sign, read as by in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: A pole turned by a dull doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter?' looks like a doorman; it is a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is a bar about which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Character fronting Savoy, reportedly magnanimous spirit

indicators.note: said aloud, the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: the capital letter opening Savoy is a large S

explanation.surface: A doorman at the Savoy hotel is said to be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital that begins 'Savoy' is a large S; spoken, 'large S' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity in giving.

clue.text: Street person heaving frame covered with canvas

parts.note: someone retching heaves as if to vomit

explanation.surface: A vomiting man in the street gets carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a canvas frame for carrying the sick or injured.

clue.text: Inexpensive pile found in county

indicators.note: the pile word is found inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A cheap pile of a house turns up in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; a cheapo is informal for a bargain-basement item.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is slang for cheap, low-cost.

clue.text: Distribute New Age pop art

indicators.note: new suggests these letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: New Age pop art being spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges AGE POP ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread widely.

clue.text: Trader delivered more fat

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so these words are spoken

parts.note: gross means very fat, so grosser is fatter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper brought round more lard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food.

clue.text: Ship about to disentangle, cutting free French one

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the French word is cut away, freeing the rest

parts.note: to unravel is to disentangle
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A ship's crew about to untangle ropes, cutting a Frenchman loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting free' takes UN from UNRAVEL, leaving RAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel is a small fast sailing ship of the 15th–16th centuries.

clue.text: Evil faceless melting apparition

parts.note: ill means bad or evil, as in ill will

indicators.note: losing its face means dropping its first letter

parts.note: fusion is melting together

explanation.surface: A wicked featureless phantom dissolving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faceless' takes F from FUSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is a false appearance, a phantom.

clue.text: Flash odds on racehorse

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at a race's start
Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s

explanation.surface: The betting on a horse called Flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places SP above ARKLE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkle is a brief flash of light.

clue.text: Order recorder of minutes to destroy minutes

indicators.note: the minutes letter is wiped out of the device word

parts.note: a timer records minutes passing

explanation.surface: The minute-taker is told to destroy the minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to destroy' removes M from TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a rank or level in an order.

clue.text: Arctic base's great facilities losing billions

indicators.note: losing means giving up a letter from the word

parts.note: big means great
loo is British slang for toilet, often called the facilities

explanation.surface: A polar station's grand toilet block costs less after billions go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes B from BIG, leaving IG.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit snow dwelling, a home base in the Arctic.

clue.text: Separated by current, sailor and woman surfacing

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the woman word is split by the current letters set within it

parts.note: madam is a woman
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A sailor and a woman kept apart by the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separated by' splits MADAM as M-AC-ADAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is a road surfacing of tar and stone.

clue.text: Like chicken pasty?

parts.note: as means like, as in as gold
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A pie made from chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like a pie; it is the adjective pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale-faced.

clue.text: Cut hard pine knot

parts.note: clove is a past tense of cleave, to cut
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to itch is to long or pine for

explanation.surface: Cutting a knot in hard pine wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a sailor's knot.

clue.text: Twitch seen at regular intervals?

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is seen

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch keeps recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of the clue's first word gives a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is a habitual spasm of the muscles.

clue.text: King leading people from the east?

definitions.text: King leading people from the east?

indicators.note: the king's letter goes in front of the people

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Han are the majority ethnic people of China

explanation.surface: A monarch at the head of an eastern nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler in Central Asia, a sovereign from the east.

clue.text: Catch enormous bird eating everything around

indicators.note: turned around, the combined word reads backwards
the bird swallows the second word inside it

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
all means everything

explanation.surface: Trapping a giant bird that devours all in its path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' makes RALLOC; 'around' then turns the whole thing back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar someone is to catch or seize them.

clue.text: Met done checking case of vice

indicators.note: checking means holding back, so the swindle word holds the letters inside

parts.note: done means swindled, conned

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: The Met police, swindled, investigate a case of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes VE, the first and last letters of vice; 'checking' puts them in CONNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to come together, so a body that convened has met.
